Zionism
/ˈzaɪ.əˌnɪ.zəm/
noun
From Zion (Hebrew צִיּוֹן Ṣiyyôn) + -ism. Modern political sense coined late 19th c. (esp. after Herzl, Der Judenstaat, 1896) for the movement seeking a national home for the Jewish people in the land of Israel. Distinct from biblical “Zion” language (place, people, eschatological hope).

Biblical Definition

Zionism, in ordinary modern usage, is the political and national movement that arose in the late nineteenth century to secure a homeland for the Jewish people in the land historically tied to Israel — culminating, as a political fact, in the modern State of Israel (1948). The Bible’s own “Zion” language is older and deeper: Zion is fortress, city of David, temple mount, Jerusalem, the covenant people, and finally the heavenly city (Ps 48; 87; Isa 2; Heb 12:22; Rev 14:1). Biblical Zion is not identical to modern political Zionism. Scripture binds the Church to love the Jewish people, tell the truth about covenant history, and refuse racial hatred; it does not baptize every modern nationalist program as the controlling key of prophecy. Isaiah’s “Israel, you will not be forgotten by Me” (Isaiah 44:21) is covenant speech to the people under God’s redemptive dealing — not a blank check for equating every contemporary geopolitical claim with the gospel.

What it is: a modern political-national project with real history, real suffering behind it (esp. European antisemitism and the Holocaust), and real consequences in the Middle East.
What it is not: automatically “the fulfillment timetable” of Daniel/Revelation; not a substitute for faith in Messiah; not a permission slip for the Church to outsource her ethics to any nation’s foreign policy; not a synonym for biblical hope in Zion.

Webster 1828 Definition

Not in Webster 1828 — modern political term (late 19th c.).

Key Scripture

Psalm 137:5-6 — "If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning. If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth; if I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy."

Isaiah 2:2-3 — "And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD'S house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it..."

Isaiah 44:21 — "Remember these, O Jacob and Israel; for thou art my servant: I have formed thee; thou art my servant: O Israel, thou shalt not be forgotten of me."

Romans 9:1-5 — "I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Ghost, That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren..."

Romans 11:1-2 — "I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel, saying,"

Romans 11:25-29 — "For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in..."

Hebrews 12:22 — "But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels,"

Galatians 4:25-26 — "For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answereth to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children. But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all."

Modern Corruption

Prophetic over-identification on one side; antisemitic smear and dual-covenant drift on the other.

expand to see more

Two opposite corruptions stalk this word. (1) Prophetic over-identification: treating the modern state as the master key of the Bible, so that charts, blood moons, and news cycles catechize the church more than Christ and the apostles. (2) Antisemitic smear: using critique of a political ideology or a government policy as cover for hatred of Jews as a people — a sin Scripture condemns and history shames. A third corruption is sentimental dualism: speaking as if Jewish unbelief no longer matters because “they’re God’s people politically,” which guts the necessity of the gospel (Romans 1:16; John 14:6). Hold the line: truth without hatred; covenant fulfillment in Christ without erasing Jewish particularity or future mercy.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Zion (Ṣiyyôn) + modern -ism; not a biblical technical system-name.

expand to see more

Hebrew צִיּוֹן (Ṣiyyôn) — Zion: fortress, ridge, city of David, temple mount, Jerusalem, and by extension the people and the eschatological hope centered there.

Modern -ism — labels an ideology/movement. Biblical Zion language predates and outruns the late-19th-century political project.

Usage

""Biblical Zion is not identical to modern political Zionism — confuse them and your eschatology will catechize you faster than Christ will.""

""Critique a policy if you must; never baptize hatred of the Jewish people as 'just anti-Zionism.'""

""Name the thing accurately. Love Jewish neighbors. Preach Christ to Jew and Gentile alike.""
